fields.narrative_intro: *A sleep-deprived person and a haughty person discuss Hacktron's OpenAI breach on a runaway train.*
fields.panel1:
[setup]
SLEEP-DEPRIVED PERSON: "Hacktron got RCE on community.openai.com through libheif's missing Debian backport."
[Visual: The train's brake is labeled “libheif”; a sticker reads “Debian security backport: missing.”]
fields.panel2:
[build]
HAUGHTY PERSON: "SSO misconfiguration hijacked employee ChatGPT and Codex accounts."
SLEEP-DEPRIVED PERSON: "Then the attackers opened a pull request inside OpenAI's private monorepo."
fields.panel3:
[pivot]
SLEEP-DEPRIVED PERSON: "Claude Opus 5 wrote the working ASLR bypass in roughly three hours."
HAUGHTY PERSON: "Anthropic's model? In a sandboxed CTF proxy to dodge safety refusals?"
fields.panel4:
[silent reaction]
[Visual: Both stare at a monitor reading “AUTHOR: CLAUDE OPUS 5”; the runaway train's throttle locks forward.]
fields.panel5:
[punch]
HAUGHTY PERSON: "So the $6,500 bounty beat an under-$3,000 token bill?"
SLEEP-DEPRIVED PERSON: "Claude became OpenAI's cheapest unpaid penetration tester."
fields.panel6:
[button]
[Visual: The emergency brake is a pull request titled “Patch libheif”; it reads “OPEN” as the train passes “UNDER 72 HOURS.”]

narrative_summary: Hacktron's libheif-to-SSO chain makes Claude Opus 5 OpenAI's cheapest unpaid penetration tester.
rationale: Candidate 3 uses the story's exact technical chain and makes the freshest comic turn: Claude becomes OpenAI's “cheapest unpaid penetration tester.” The runaway-train metaphor is reinforced by the pull-request emergency brake, giving the ending a stronger visual and verbal payoff than the more straightforward cost recap in Candidates 1 and 2.
story_title: A heap overflow and SSO misconfiguration to compromise OpenAI internal repos
hat_pair: foam cloud hat with a tiny plastic rain shower dangling below the brim
